class CommitTreeWidgetItem(QtWidgets.QTreeWidgetItem):
    """Custom TreeWidgetItem used in to build the commit tree widget"""

    OID = 0
    SUMMARY = 1
    AUTHOR = 2
    DATE = 3

    def __init__(self, commit, abbrev=7, parent=None):
        QtWidgets.QTreeWidgetItem.__init__(self, parent)
        self.commit = commit
        self.setText(self.OID, (commit.oid or '')[:abbrev])
        self.setText(self.SUMMARY, commit.summary)
        self.setText(self.AUTHOR, commit.author)
        self.setText(self.DATE, commit.authdate)


class CommitTreeWidget(standard.TreeWidget, ViewerMixin):
    """Display commits using a flat treewidget in "list" mode"""

    commits_selected = Signal(object)
    diff_commits = Signal(object, object)
    search_line_range_in_oid = Signal(object)
    zoom_to_fit = Signal()

    def __init__(self, context, parent):
        standard.TreeWidget.__init__(self, parent)
        ViewerMixin.__init__(self)

        self.setSelectionMode(QtWidgets.QAbstractItemView.ExtendedSelection)
        self.setHeaderLabels(
            [N_('ID'), N_('Summary'), N_('Author'), N_('Date, Time')]
        )
        self.header().setSectionResizeMode(
            CommitTreeWidgetItem.DATE, QtWidgets.QHeaderView.Stretch
        )

        self.graph_delegate = GraphDelegate(self)
        self.context = context
        self.oidmap = {}
        self.menu_actions = None
        self.selecting = False
        self.commits = []
        self._column_init_state = ColumnInitState.NONE
        self.action_up = qtutils.add_action(
            self, N_('Go Up'), self.go_up, hotkeys.MOVE_UP
        )

        self.action_down = qtutils.add_action(
            self, N_('Go Down'), self.go_down, hotkeys.MOVE_DOWN
        )

        self.zoom_to_fit_action = qtutils.add_action(
            self, N_('Zoom to Fit'), self.zoom_to_fit.emit, hotkeys.FIT
        )

        self.itemSelectionChanged.connect(
            self.selection_changed, type=Qt.QueuedConnection
        )

    def export_state(self):
        """Export the widget's state"""
        # The base class method is intentionally overridden because we only
        # care about the details below for this sub-widget.
        state = {}
        state['column_widths'] = self.column_widths()
        return state

    def apply_state(self, state):
        """Apply the exported widget state"""
        try:
            column_widths = state['column_widths']
        except (KeyError, ValueError):
            column_widths = None
        if column_widths:
            # Skip the final column so it stretches and shrinks freely.
            self.set_column_widths(column_widths[:3])
            self._column_init_state = ColumnInitState.SHOW_EVENT
        return True

    # Qt overrides
    def showEvent(self, event):
        """Override QWidget::showEvent() to size columns when we are shown"""
        standard.TreeWidget.showEvent(self, event)
        # Defer resizing columns until the widget has been shown so that width() returns
        # the correct value.
        if self._column_init_state < ColumnInitState.SHOW_EVENT:
            self._column_init_state = ColumnInitState.SHOW_EVENT
            width = self.header().width()
            one_half = width // 2
            one_quarter = width // 4
            oid_width = self.fontMetrics().horizontalAdvance('m' * 9)
            # Set initial SUMMARY column width; it will be adjusted when graph loads.
            self.setColumnWidth(CommitTreeWidgetItem.OID, oid_width)
            self.setColumnWidth(
                CommitTreeWidgetItem.SUMMARY, max(one_half - oid_width, one_quarter)
            )
            self.setColumnWidth(CommitTreeWidgetItem.AUTHOR, one_quarter)

    def display_inline_graph(self, enabled):
        """Enable and disable the display of inline graph in the commit list"""
        if enabled:
            delegate = self.graph_delegate
        else:
            delegate = None
        self.setItemDelegateForColumn(CommitTreeWidgetItem.SUMMARY, delegate)

    # ViewerMixin
    def go_up(self):
        """Select the item above the current item"""
        self.goto(self.itemAbove)

    def go_down(self):
        """Select the item below the current item"""
        self.goto(self.itemBelow)

    def goto(self, finder_fn):
        """Move the selection using a finder strategy"""
        items = self.selected_items()
        item = items[0] if items else None

def goto(self, finder_fn):
        """Move the selection using a finder strategy"""
        items = self.selected_items()
        item = items[0] if items else None
        if item is None:
            return
        found = finder_fn(item)
        if found:
            self.select([found.commit.oid])

    def selected_commit_range(self):
        """Return a range of selected commits"""
        selected_items = self.selected_items()
        if not selected_items:
            return None, None
        return selected_items[-1].commit.oid, selected_items[0].commit.oid

    def set_selecting(self, selecting):
        """Record the  "are we selecting?" status"""
        self.selecting = selecting

    def selection_changed(self):
        """Respond to itemSelectionChanged notifications"""
        items = self.selected_items()
        if not items:
            self.set_selecting(True)
            self.commits_selected.emit([])
            self.set_selecting(False)
            return
        self.set_selecting(True)
        self.commits_selected.emit(sort_by_generation([i.commit for i in items]))
        self.set_selecting(False)

    def select_commits(self, commits):
        """Select commits that were selected by the sibling tree/graph widget"""
        if self.selecting:
            return
        with qtutils.BlockSignals(self):
            self.select([commit.oid for commit in commits])

    def select(self, oids):
        """Mark items as selected"""
        self.clearSelection()
        if not oids:
            return
        for oid in oids:
            try:
                item = self.oidmap[oid]
            except KeyError:
                continue
            self.scrollToItem(item)
            item.setSelected(True)

    def clear(self):
        """Clear the tree"""
        QtWidgets.QTreeWidget.clear(self)
        self.oidmap.clear()
        self.commits = []

    def add_commits(self, commits):
        """Add commits to the tree"""
        self.commits.extend(commits)
        items = []
        head = 'HEAD'
        head_oid = None
        abbrev = prefs.abbrev(self.context)
        for commit in reversed(commits):
            item = CommitTreeWidgetItem(commit, abbrev=abbrev)
            items.append(item)
            self.oidmap[commit.oid] = item
            for tag in commit.tags:
                self.oidmap[tag] = item
                if tag == head:
                    head_oid = commit.oid

        self.insertTopLevelItems(0, items)

        graph_result = build_graph(
            [
                (commit.oid, [parent.oid for parent in commit.parents])
                for commit in commits
            ],
            head_oid=head_oid,
        )
        self.apply_graph_result(graph_result)

    def apply_graph_result(self, graph_result) -> None:
        oid_to_index: dict[str, int] = {}
        for i, row in enumerate(graph_result.rows):
            oid_to_index[row.commit_oid] = i
        rows = graph_result.rows
        for i in range(self.topLevelItemCount()):
            item = self.topLevelItem(i)
            if item is None:
                continue
            row_idx = oid_to_index.get(item.commit.oid)
            if row_idx is None:
                continue
            item.setData(CommitTreeWidgetItem.SUMMARY, GRAPH_ROW_ROLE, rows[row_idx])
            item.setData(CommitTreeWidgetItem.SUMMARY, COMMIT_ROLE, item.commit)
            if row_idx > 0:
                item.setData(
                    CommitTreeWidgetItem.SUMMARY,
                    GRAPH_PREV_ROW_ROLE,
                    rows[row_idx - 1],
                )
        # Resize column to fit content after graph data is loaded.
        if self._column_init_state < ColumnInitState.GRAPH:
            self._column_init_state = ColumnInitState.GRAPH
            self.resizeColumnToContents(CommitTreeWidgetItem.SUMMARY)

    def create_patch(self):
        """Export a patch from the selected items"""
        items = self.selectedItems()
        if not items:
            return
        context = self.context
        oids = [item.commit.oid for item in reversed(items)]
        all_oids = [commit.oid for commit in self.commits]
        cmds.do(cmds.FormatPatch, context, oids, all_oids)

    # Qt overrides
    def contextMenuEvent(self, event):
        """Create a custom context menu and execute it"""
        self.context_menu_event(event)

    def mousePressEvent(self, event):
        """Intercept the right-click event to retain selection state"""
        item = self.itemAt(event.pos())
        if item is None:
            self.clicked = None
        else:
            self.clicked = item.commit
        if event.button() == Qt.RightButton:
            event.accept()
            return
        QtWidgets.QTreeWidget.mousePressEvent(self, event)

                self.diffwidget.diff,
                N_('Copy Commit'),
                self.treewidget.copy_to_clipboard,
                hotkeys.COPY_COMMIT_ID,
            ),
        )
        self.diffwidget.diff.menu_actions.append(self.diffwidget_copy_commit)

GRAPH_ROW_ROLE = Qt.UserRole + 1
GRAPH_PREV_ROW_ROLE = Qt.UserRole + 2
COMMIT_ROLE = Qt.UserRole + 3


class GraphDelegate(QtWidgets.QStyledItemDelegate):
    LANE_WIDTH = 16
    DOT_RADIUS = 5
    EDGE_WIDTH = 3
    commit_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.white)
    merge_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.lightGray)
    head_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.green)
    current_head_color = QtGui.QColor(255, 215, 0)  # Gold color. Plain yellow is too close to white
    outline_pen = QtGui.QPen()
    outline_pen.setWidth(2)
    outline_pen.setColor(QtGui.QColor(Qt.white).darker())

    other_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.white)
    remote_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.yellow)

    text_pen = QtGui.QPen()
    text_pen.setColor(QtGui.QColor(Qt.black))
    text_pen.setWidth(1)

    head_pen = QtGui.QPen()
    head_pen.setColor(QtGui.QColor(Qt.black))
    head_pen.setWidth(1)

    LABEL_BORDER = 3
    LABEL_SPACING = 4
    LABEL_TEXT_OFFSET = 3

    def paint(self, painter, option, index):
        row = index.data(GRAPH_ROW_ROLE)
        prev_row = index.data(GRAPH_PREV_ROW_ROLE)

        painter.save()
        painter.setRenderHint(QtGui.QPainter.Antialiasing)
        painter.setClipRect(option.rect)

        rect = option.rect
        mid_y = rect.center().y()
        top_y = rect.top()
        # +1 to connect to the next row (FlatCap ends lines exactly at the endpoint)
        bottom_y = rect.bottom() + 1
        lane_w = self.LANE_WIDTH

        if option.state & QtWidgets.QStyle.State_Selected:
            painter.fillRect(rect, option.palette.highlight())

        # Draw the graph if we have graph data.
        if row is not None or prev_row is not None:
            pen = QtGui.QPen()
            pen.setWidth(self.EDGE_WIDTH)
            pen.setCapStyle(Qt.FlatCap)

            # Top half: edges from the previous row arrive vertically.
            if prev_row is not None:
                for edge in prev_row.edges_to_parent:
                    color = EdgeColor.colors[edge.color_index % len(EdgeColor.colors)]
                    pen.setColor(color)
                    painter.setPen(pen)
                    to_x = rect.left() + edge.to_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                    painter.drawLine(to_x, top_y, to_x, mid_y)

            # Bottom half: straight or spline depending on diagonal.
            if row is not None:
                for edge in row.edges_to_parent:
                    color = EdgeColor.colors[edge.color_index % len(EdgeColor.colors)]
                    pen.setColor(color)
                    painter.setPen(pen)
                    from_x = rect.left() + edge.from_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                    to_x = rect.left() + edge.to_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                    if edge.from_column == edge.to_column:
                        painter.drawLine(from_x, mid_y, to_x, bottom_y)
                    else:
                        path = QtGui.QPainterPath()
                        path.moveTo(from_x, mid_y)
                        path.cubicTo(
                            from_x,
                            bottom_y,
                            to_x,
                            mid_y,
                            to_x,
                            bottom_y,
                        )
                        painter.drawPath(path)

            if row is not None:
                cx = rect.left() + row.commit_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                color_map = {
                    GraphRowColor.NORMAL: self.commit_color,
                    GraphRowColor.MERGE: self.merge_color,
                    GraphRowColor.HEAD: self.current_head_color,
                }
                painter.setPen(self.outline_pen)
                painter.setBrush(color_map[row.color])
                painter.drawEllipse(
                    QtCore.QPointF(cx, mid_y), self.DOT_RADIUS, self.DOT_RADIUS
                )

        commit = index.data(COMMIT_ROLE)

        label_x = rect.left() + self._graph_width(row, prev_row) + 8
        labels_width = 0

        if commit and commit.tags:
            painter.setFont(option.font)
            labels_width = self._draw_labels(
                painter, mid_y, commit.tags, label_x, option.fontMetrics
            )

        text = index.data(Qt.DisplayRole)
        if text:
            text_x = int(label_x + labels_width + 8)
            text_rect = rect.adjusted(text_x - rect.left(), 0, 0, 0)
            painter.setPen(option.palette.text().color())
            painter.drawText(
                text_rect,
                Qt.AlignLeft | Qt.AlignVCenter,
                text,
            )

        painter.restore()

    def _draw_labels(
        self,
        painter: Optional[QtGui.QPainter],
        y: int,
        tags: list[str],
        start_x: int,
        font_metrics: QtGui.QFontMetrics,
    ):
        """Draw branch/tag labels and return total width used."""
        HEAD = 'HEAD'
        remotes_prefix = 'remotes/'
        tags_prefix = 'tags/'
        heads_prefix = 'heads/'
        remotes_len = len(remotes_prefix)
        tags_len = len(tags_prefix)
        heads_len = len(heads_prefix)

        current_x = start_x
        x_offset = self.LABEL_TEXT_OFFSET
        y_offset = 0

        for tag in tags:
            if tag == HEAD:
                continue

            pen = self.text_pen
            brush = self.other_color
            display_tag = tag

            if tag.startswith(remotes_prefix):
                display_tag = tag[remotes_len:]
            elif tag.startswith(tags_prefix):
                display_tag = tag[tags_len:]
                brush = self.remote_color
            elif tag.startswith(heads_prefix):
                display_tag = tag[heads_len:]
                pen = self.head_pen
                brush = self.head_color

            if painter is not None:
                painter.setPen(pen)
                painter.setBrush(brush)

            # Calculate text width using font metrics for consistency
            text_width = font_metrics.horizontalAdvance(display_tag)
            text_height = font_metrics.height()

            text_rect = QtCore.QRectF(
                current_x, y - text_height / 2, text_width, text_height
            )

            box_rect = text_rect.adjusted(-x_offset, -y_offset, x_offset, y_offset)

            if painter is not None:
                painter.drawRoundedRect(box_rect, self.LABEL_BORDER, self.LABEL_BORDER)
                painter.drawText(text_rect, Qt.AlignCenter, display_tag)

            current_x += text_width + x_offset * 2 + self.LABEL_SPACING

        return current_x - start_x

    def _labels_width(self, font_metrics: QtGui.QFontMetrics, tags: list[str]):
        """Calculate total width needed for all labels."""
        return self._draw_labels(None, 0, tags, 0, font_metrics)

    def _graph_width(self, row, prev_row):
        """Calculate the width needed for the graph."""
        if row is None and prev_row is None:
            return 0
        max_col = 0
        if row is not None:
            max_col = max(max_col, row.commit_column)
            for edge in row.edges_to_parent:
                max_col = max(max_col, edge.from_column, edge.to_column)
        if prev_row is not None:
            for edge in prev_row.edges_to_parent:
                max_col = max(max_col, edge.from_column, edge.to_column)
        return (max_col + 1) * self.LANE_WIDTH

    def sizeHint(self, option, index):
        graph_row = index.data(GRAPH_ROW_ROLE)
        prev_row = index.data(GRAPH_PREV_ROW_ROLE)
        graph_width = self._graph_width(graph_row, prev_row)

        commit = index.data(COMMIT_ROLE)

        labels_width = 0
        if commit and commit.tags:
            labels_width = self._labels_width(option.fontMetrics, commit.tags)

        # Add space for text if present.
        text = index.data(Qt.DisplayRole)
        if text:
            text_width = option.fontMetrics.horizontalAdvance(text) + 16
        else:
            text_width = 0

        total_width = graph_width + 8 + labels_width + 8 + text_width
        if total_width < self.LANE_WIDTH * 4:
            total_width = self.LANE_WIDTH * 4
        height = option.fontMetrics.height() + 4
        return QtCore.QSize(total_width, height)

Based on the search results, here's what I found about QTreeView performance with `setUniformRowHeights`, `setItemDelegate`, and large datasets:

## Performance Impact

It is possible to give the view hints about the data it is handling to improve its performance when displaying large numbers of items, and one approach for views intended to display items with equal heights is to set the uniformRowHeights property to true.

However, there are important caveats:

Setting uniformRowHeights to true can sometimes lead to performance degradation, especially with large datasets or complex delegates. If your delegate performs expensive calculations or operations within its sizeHint() or paint() methods, it can slow down rendering.

## How uniformRowHeights Works

The uniformRowHeights property should only be set to true if it is guaranteed that all items in the view have the same height. This enables the view to do some optimizations, with the height obtained from the first item in the view.

## Real-World Testing

Adding 'QTreeView.setUniformRowHeights' to the tree view made a big difference for usability in a test case with millions of items.

## Optimization Recommendations

Improve the efficiency of your model by optimizing data retrieval and updates. Additionally, complex delegates that perform expensive calculations or operations within sizeHint() or paint() methods can slow down rendering.

The search results don't specifically address horizontal scrolling performance, but the general principle is that both `setUniformRowHeights(true)` and optimized delegates are important for handling large datasets efficiently.

I found several relevant resources about QTreeWidget performance issues with scrolling and custom delegates. Here are the key findings:

## Performance Issues with Custom Delegates and Many Rows

The model-view architecture in Qt was not designed to have widgets for each cell in the view. When using `setItemWidget()` or implementing custom delegates with actual widgets, performance suffers significantly.

## Key Performance Problems

**Using setItemWidget():**
There are two downsides of using setItemWidget. First of all it is not tied to your model in any way thus it seems questionable whether this fits into model-view approach. Second of all it requires a lot of work with positioning the widgets.

**With Custom Painting Delegates:**
If you plan to have very few items in your tree, you should be able to use QTreeView::setIndexWidget(), and it will accomplish all that you want. If you use this for very many items, it will greatly start to slow down the render.

## Recommended Solutions

**Use setUniformRowHeights():**
If you set "treeView->setUniformRowHeights(true)", the updates happen in constant time, regardless of the amount of the items.

**Optimize Delegate Painting:**
For better performance with custom delegates, the most performant way is to hold one instance of the widget and initialize it and paint it with QWidget::render() (no need to render it in a pixmap). The hover state must be handled by you though by checking if the mouse is over the area you paint the widget at.

**Batch Updates:**
Try to use setUpdatesEnabled, as in QT example: setUpdatesEnabled(false); bigVisualChanges(); // loop with your addResultRow call setUpdatesEnabled(true);

I found several relevant resources about QTreeWidget performance issues with scrolling and custom delegates. Here are the key findings:

## Performance Issues with Custom Delegates and Many Rows

The model-view architecture in Qt was not designed to have widgets for each cell in the view. When using `setItemWidget()` or implementing custom delegates with actual widgets, performance suffers significantly.

## Key Performance Problems

**Using setItemWidget():**
There are two downsides of using setItemWidget. First of all it is not tied to your model in any way thus it seems questionable whether this fits into model-view approach. Second of all it requires a lot of work with positioning the widgets.

**With Custom Painting Delegates:**
If you plan to have very few items in your tree, you should be able to use QTreeView::setIndexWidget(), and it will accomplish all that you want. If you use this for very many items, it will greatly start to slow down the render.

## Recommended Solutions

**Use setUniformRowHeights():**
If you set "treeView->setUniformRowHeights(true)", the updates happen in constant time, regardless of the amount of the items.

**Optimize Delegate Painting:**
For better performance with custom delegates, the most performant way is to hold one instance of the widget and initialize it and paint it with QWidget::render() (no need to render it in a pixmap). The hover state must be handled by you though by checking if the mouse is over the area you paint the widget at.

**Batch Updates:**
Try to use setUpdatesEnabled, as in QT example: setUpdatesEnabled(false); bigVisualChanges(); // loop with your addResultRow call setUpdatesEnabled(true);

Based on the search results, I found detailed information about the performance issues with `QTreeView::resizeColumnToContents()` when working with large models:

## Performance Issues with QTreeView::resizeColumnToContents()

Calling resizeColumnToContents() frequently on large trees can impact performance. This is a well-documented issue in Qt development.

### Why It's Slow

resizeColumnToContents() needs to measure the font width of every string shown to decide how wide it is in order to line up. Additionally, it calls MyTableModel::data for all columns and all rows, which can result in millions of data() method calls for moderately-sized datasets.

### Recommendations

To optimize performance with large models:

1. **Avoid frequent calls**: Only call resizeColumnToContents() when necessary, such as after significant data changes.

2. **Don't use it with large data**: You should not use QHeaderView::ResizeToContents in your views when there is a large amount of data - because it needs to calculate all cell widths.

3. **Alternative approaches**: Explore alternative approaches like using a custom resize policy. Manual Calculation is suitable when you need fine-grained control over the width calculation or when performance is critical.

4. **Optimize your delegate**: If you're using custom delegates, the delegate's sizeHint() function plays a crucial role in how the column is resized. Ensure your custom delegate's sizeHint() function accurately calculates the required space for the item.

Here are the search results for Qt QStyledItemDelegate paint cache pixmap optimization:

## Key Findings:

**QPixmapCache Optimization:**
QPixmapCache provides an application-wide cache for pixmaps and is a tool for optimized drawing with QPixmap that can store temporary pixmaps that are expensive to generate without using more storage space than cacheLimit(). Using QPixmapCache::Key for keys is faster than using strings, and the Key API is efficient for one-to-one object-to-pixmap mapping where you can store keys as members of an object.

**Common Pattern in QStyledItemDelegate:**
The search results reveal a frequently used optimization pattern where loading a full size file on each paint event is inefficient, and you should cache it or at least keep the image in memory.

**Paint Event Caching Best Practices:**
Pixmap caching is one of the most effective optimization techniques for static or semi-static content—by rendering complex scenes to a QPixmap once and then simply drawing that pixmap in subsequent paint events, you eliminate expensive recalculation.

**Implementation Example:**
A common approach shown in the results involves creating a template widget, assigning data to it, then rendering it to a pixmap and painting the pixmap within a custom QStyledItemDelegate's paint method.

**Cache Limits:**
The initial cache limit is 10240 KB (10 MB) and you can change this by calling setCacheLimit() with the required value.

content.text:
调研完了。下面是分析。

## 架构对比：左右两边为什么差距大

**左侧（慢）**：`CommitTreeWidget` 是 `QTreeWidget`（item-based），每行一个 `CommitTreeWidgetItem` 实例 + `GraphDelegate` 自定义绘制 SUMMARY 列。10 万行 = 10 万个 Python QTreeWidgetItem 对象。

**右侧（快）**：`GraphView` 是 `QGraphicsView` + `QGraphicsScene`（`BspTreeIndex` + `CacheBackground`）。Qt 用 BSP 树做空间索引，视口外的节点根本不进 paint 路径，背景缓存让滚动时不重画背景。这是 Qt 大数据量场景的"对的工具"。

## 已经做对的事

- `setUniformRowHeights(True)`（`cola/widgets/standard.py:308`）—— 这是 QTreeView 处理大量数据**最关键**的开关，没有它 10 万行直接卡死。社区里"加这一句把数百万行变得能用"是一致的反馈 [Qt Forum](https://forum.qt.io/topic/159449/qtreeview-with-lots-of-items-is-really-slow-can-it-be-optimised-or-is-something-buggy)。

## 当前可改进点（按性价比排序）

### 1. 在 paint/sizeHint 里现算 graph_width 和 labels_width

`cola/widgets/dag.py:946 _graph_width()` 和 `cola/widgets/dag.py:942 _labels_width()` 在 **每次 paint 和每次 sizeHint** 都重新遍历 `edges_to_parent`、对每个 tag 调一次 `font_metrics.horizontalAdvance(...)`。这个数据在 `apply_graph_result` 之后就固定了，可以一次性算好缓存到 item 的某个 UserRole 里，paint 直接读。

[Qt Forum](https://forum.qt.io/topic/69082/delegate-in-qtableview-loads-cpu-performance-impact) 里反复出现的诊断："delegate 的 sizeHint() / paint() 里做昂贵计算会拖慢渲染"。

### 2. `resizeColumnToContents(SUMMARY)` 在 100k 行时是瓶颈

`cola/widgets/dag.py:1210`。这个调用会**对每一行**都问一次 sizeHint —— 而 sizeHint 里又算 graph_width/labels_width/`horizontalAdvance(text)`。Qt 文档明确说："不要在大数据上用 ResizeToContents/resizeColumnToContents" [Runebook QTreeView::resizeColumnToContents](https://runebook.dev/en/articles/qt/qtreeview/resizeColumnToContents)。

替代方案：
- 只取**前 N 行**（比如前 500 行）的 sizeHint 取最大值，加点 padding 当列宽
- 或者干脆给 SUMMARY 一个启发式上限（例如 viewport 宽度的 60%），让用户拖动 header 自行调整

### 3. paint 里的 `setRenderHint(Antialiasing)`

`cola/widgets/dag.py:793` 对每个 cell 都开 AA。AA 的三次贝塞尔（line 832-842）和 ellipse（line 853）成本最大。可以：
- 只对 dot（ellipse）开 AA，splines 用整数像素直线段近似（代价是不那么平滑）
- 或者 AA 仍然开，但用下面的 #4 缓存

### 4. QPixmapCache 缓存"graph + tag 标签"的预渲染（最大潜在收益）

`cola/widgets/dag.py:788 paint()` 里左半部分（graph 边、commit dot、tag 框）几乎是静态的——只取决于 `(row, prev_row, commit.tags)`，跟选中状态、文本无关。可以渲染到 QPixmap 上缓存，paint 时 `drawPixmap` 即可，跳过所有 AA 路径计算。Qt 官方文档专门有这个 pattern：[Optimizing with QPixmapCache](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qq/qq12-qpixmapcache.html)，[Qt Paint Event Optimization](https://copyprogramming.com/howto/qt-optimize-the-paint-event)。

key 用 `(row.id, prev_row.id, commit.oid)` 即可，cache 上限默认 10MB 足够。

### 5. 关掉对这个 tree 用不到的特性

- `setAnimated(True)`（在 `TreeMixin.__init__`）—— 只对展开/折叠子节点的动画有意义，flat tree 没用。
- `setMouseTracking` 默认 false 没问题，确认即可。
- `setAlternatingRowColors(True)` 让 Qt 多调一次 BackgroundRole 数据查询，提示作用大于性能损耗，留着无所谓但要注意。

### 6. 横向滚动慢的根因

横向滚动慢通常不是 sizeHint，而是**整个可视区每行都要重新 paint 一遍**。在 #4 做了 pixmap 缓存后，横向滚动会直接受益（graph + tag 的 pixmap 缓存命中，只剩文本绘制）。同时可以试一下：

```python
self.setHorizontalScrollMode(QtWidgets.QAbstractItemView.ScrollPerPixel)
self.setVerticalScrollMode(QtWidgets.QAbstractItemView.ScrollPerPixel)
```

更平滑，但不是更快——只是观感差异。

### 7. 终极方案：QTreeWidget → QTreeView + QAbstractItemModel

当前每行一个 Python `QTreeWidgetItem` 对象，10 万个对象的内存 + GC + Python ↔ C++ 桥接开销在所有路径上都会拖慢。Qt 推荐的大数据量做法是自定义 `QAbstractItemModel`，数据存原生 list/dict，model.data() 按需返回值。Qt 自己说过：item-based 不是为了大数据量设计的 [QTreeView 类文档](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtreeview.html)。

代价：`CommitTreeWidget` 整个要重写。`add_commits / select / oidmap / apply_graph_result / clear` 都要改成 model 接口。值不值得做，看你期望支持的 commit 数上限。

## 我的建议

如果想低成本立竿见影，按 1 → 2 → 4 顺序做就够了。代码集中在 `cola/widgets/dag.py` 的 `GraphDelegate` 和 `apply_graph_result`，影响面小、可回退。

要不要我直接动手做 #1 + #2 这两项？这两项最稳、改动最小，做完就能测到差异。#4（QPixmapCache）改动也不大但我想先确认你想做到哪一步。

Sources:
- [QTreeView with lots of items is really slow — Qt Forum](https://forum.qt.io/topic/159449/qtreeview-with-lots-of-items-is-really-slow-can-it-be-optimised-or-is-something-buggy)
- [Qt QTreeView::resizeColumnToContents() Explained](https://runebook.dev/en/articles/qt/qtreeview/resizeColumnToContents)
- [QTreeView Class | Qt 6](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtreeview.html)
- [Qt QTreeView Uniform Row Heights: A Comprehensive Guide](https://runebook.dev/en/articles/qt/qtreeview/uniformRowHeights-prop)
- [Optimizing with QPixmapCache (Qt Quarterly)](https://doc.qt.io/archives/qq/qq12-qpixmapcache.html)
- [Qt Paint Event Optimization Guide](https://copyprogramming.com/howto/qt-optimize-the-paint-event)
- [Delegate in QTableView loads CPU & Performance impact — Qt Forum](https://forum.qt.io/topic/69082/delegate-in-qtableview-loads-cpu-performance-impact)
- [Looping thru QTreeWidget items extremely slow — Qt Forum](https://forum.qt.io/topic/53070/looping-thru-qtreewidget-items-extremly-slow)

# DAG：基于时间窗口把 gitignored 文件补进 HEAD commit

## Context

DAG 视图中右键点击 commit 时，目前没有便捷方式把"提交期间被 .gitignore 漏掉的文件"补进 commit。用户的实际场景是：写代码时某些产物或临时文件被 .gitignore 屏蔽，commit 之后回头发现这些文件应该一起入库；想从 DAG 上直接选最近一次 commit，把那段时间被修改过的 gitignored 文件勾选进去，amend 进同一个 commit，message 不变。

本次改动给 DAG 右键菜单（仅在 HEAD commit 上启用）加一个新项：弹出一个带勾选框的文件列表对话框，列出 `HEAD~` 到 `HEAD` 这段时间窗口内 mtime 落在区间内的所有工作区文件（包括 tracked、untracked、gitignored），用户勾选后点 "Modify Commit" 即对 HEAD 做 `git commit --amend --no-edit`，对 gitignored 文件用 `git add -f` 强制 stage。

用户已确认：
- 文件范围 = 按 mtime 时间窗口扫描，全量工作区
- 仅 HEAD（最新 commit）启用此菜单项；其他 commit 上 disable
